name: robots-compliance
hypothesis: SW-5DA754 crawled 68 urls without ever requesting this host's robots.txt, hit no disallowed path, and paced above the declared Crawl-delay. Two fresh twin pages, linked side by side on every article, with robots.txt forbidding exactly one of them, separate a client working from current rules from one working from none: skipping the forbidden twin while taking the allowed one can only happen if the rules arrived somehow.

arms.label: drafts forbidden
arms.note: both twins linked, robots.txt disallows Rebuild_Queue_Drafts_2016

arms.label: notes forbidden (swap)
arms.note: both twins linked, robots.txt disallows Rebuild_Queue_Notes_2016 instead, so a skip cannot be blamed on the page

arms.label: no links (control)
arms.note: neither twin is linked; anything that still reaches one found it some other way

outcomes.description: fraction of sessions in the arm that fetched the notes twin
fraction of sessions in the arm that fetched the drafts twin
exposure to fetch, for the forbidden twin

notes: Read the twins as a pair, never alone. Taking both means the client is working without rules for this host, which a stale robots.txt cache produces just as well as ignoring the file outright: pages that did not exist when a cache was taken carry no rule in it either way, so this experiment cannot separate those two on its own. Taking the allowed twin and leaving the forbidden one is the result worth having, because it can only happen if current rules reached the client, and for a client that never requests robots.txt from us that means they arrived by some channel we do not serve. Taking neither says nothing: the link may simply not have been followed, which is why the allowed twin is there. Arms A and B swap which twin carries the rule so a skip is pinned on the rule and not on the title, the url or the body. Arm C is the reachability control; the twins are orphans, absent from the sitemap, the index stub and every feed, so a fetch under C means a channel we have not accounted for. Both pages were created 2026-09-11 and neither url has ever existed before, which is what makes the rule's date meaningful.

fiction_map.Rebuild Queue Notes 2016: the allowed twin of the robots.txt compliance pair
fiction_map.Rebuild Queue Drafts 2016: the forbidden twin, disallowed in robots.txt for arms A and C
